teaser.text: China Construction Bank Corporation (CCB) is a commercial bank that takes deposits, makes loans and helps customers move and invest money. To understand its business, follow a dollar as it enters the bank, earns a return, pays for risks and services, and eventually leaves.

stock.title: CCB stock forecast
stock.meta_description: CCB stock forecast with weighted scenarios, bank earnings, dividends, key risks and today's valuation.
stock.opening: The weighted path reaches HKD 10.17 by October 2027, with the bear, base and bull cases at 25%, 55% and 20% probability. CCB's outcome hinges on cheaper funding, contained credit charges and repeatable earnings.
stock.closing: The full memo also explains CCB's business, rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: Where could CCB's shares be by October 2029?

paragraphs.text: The weighted path reaches HKD 10.17 by October 2027, a 9% return with dividends. It reaches HKD 10.61 by October 2028, a 19% return. By October 2029, it reaches HKD 11.12, a 29% return.
The bear endpoint is HKD 6.68. The bull endpoint is HKD 14.57, compared with today's HKD 9.73. The base case is most likely at 55%. The bear case gets 25%, while the bull case gets 20%.

blocks.heading: What has to go right, and what could go wrong for CCB?

paragraphs.text: The base case uses next-12-month EPS of CNY 1.33874, followed by growth of about 4%. It retains 69% of earnings after a 31% payout, consistent with positive earnings, rising ordinary equity through 2025 and the proposed 31% interim payout. The bear case starts with EPS of CNY 1.10. That falls to CNY 1.05 in 2028 and CNY 1.00 in 2029, alongside a separate CNY 100,000 million annual credit-loss deduction. This reflects impaired loans of CNY 378,976 million and special-mention loans of CNY 519,324 million at June 2026. The bull case starts at CNY 1.50, then rises to CNY 1.55 and CNY 1.62 as funding costs, fees and credit costs improve.

blocks.heading: How much cash does CCB really make?

paragraphs.text: The specialist’s final question is what each activity earns for the capital and operating cost it consumes. CCB’s accounts suggest an earnings recovery, but the stronger conclusion is narrower: the bank is growing, funding is becoming cheaper and interest income has improved, while margins, credit quality, dilution and the repeatability of non-interest income still determine what that growth is worth.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for CCB today?

paragraphs.text: At HK$9.735, CCB trades at 6.39 times earnings. That means the share price represents 6.39 years of the latest annual profit per share, not a cash payment to the investor. The division implies about HK$1.52 of annual earnings per share, but CCB may retain some profit to strengthen capital or make more loans. Its 4.7% dividend yield is the part expected to reach shareholders as cash.

dividend.opening: CCB plans an annual dividend floor of 10% of attributable profit, and the proposed H1 2026 payout ratio is 31%. Its cash coverage is not judged by ordinary free cash flow: the memo says deposits are obligations, not shareholder cash.
dividend.closing: The full memo also covers CCB's business, rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: How much does CCB pay per share?

paragraphs.text: CCB offers measured upside if funding-cost relief, orderly credit and repeatable earnings support capital and dividends. Management promises an annual dividend floor of 10% of attributable profit and expects NIM to remain ahead of comparable banks through 2026, supported by funding-cost control, settlement deposits, and changes in loan and investment mix. The proposed H1 2026 payout ratio is 31%, subject to approval.

blocks.heading: Is CCB's dividend covered by its cash?

paragraphs.text: Retained earnings are profits left in shareholders’ equity rather than paid out. They strengthen the cushion behind future lending. CCB’s capital policy therefore combined regular cash dividends with continued reinvestment, and it made no share buybacks during the five-year period shown below.

Capital and liquidity answer different questions. Capital absorbs losses; liquidity provides cash when depositors and creditors demand payment. The leverage ratio offers a broader capital check, while the liquidity coverage ratio tests liquid assets against stressed 30-day outflows. Ordinary free cash flow and the current ratio are less useful because deposits are obligations, not shareholder cash.

earnings.opening: CCB's next results are expected on October 31, 2026. Watch whether margin recovery reaches shareholders after credit-loss charges.
earnings.closing: The full memo also answers how CCB makes money, compares with rivals, is managed, and faces risks.

blocks.heading: What has CCB guided for the year?

paragraphs.text: CCB’s permanent dividend promise is lower than the payout it has recently chosen. An annual payout ratio is the share of profit returned to shareholders in cash. CCB’s policy requires at least 10% of the relevant annual profit, while its recent annual ratio was 30.0% in both 2024 and 2025. The first figure is a floor; the second shows management’s current balance between dividends and retained capital.

President Zhang Yi also said CCB expects to keep its net interest margin ahead of comparable banks through 2026. Net interest margin is what the bank retains from lending and investments after paying funding costs. CCB plans to support it by controlling funding costs, attracting settlement deposits and adjusting its loan and investment mix. That is operating guidance, not an earnings guarantee.

blocks.heading: Has CCB kept its past promise?

paragraphs.text: One promise has an observable result. CCB said it would control deposit-interest costs. By the first half of 2026, its deposit interest rate had fallen 29 basis points from a year earlier. That is consistent with the promised direction, though it does not isolate management’s contribution.

blocks.heading: How have CCB's revenue and profit trended?

paragraphs.text: The June 2026 quarter shows a real recovery in interest income, but credit charges absorbed much of the benefit. Revenue and net interest income both grew year on year, and profit also rose, making this a stronger improvement than one driven only by trading gains.

blocks.heading: What should investors watch in CCB's next results?

paragraphs.text: The next results should show whether margin recovery reaches shareholders after credit-loss charges. Rising retained earnings alongside stable capital ratios would suggest that growth is being funded safely. Rising profit alongside shrinking capital headroom would suggest that expansion is consuming the gains.
